upstream.scope: User threads and kernel-thread visibility: thread-aware source records kept apart from process records, a thread identity of its process instance plus its own TID and creation token, two independent standard checkbox Toggles with a threads status, thread rows after their process in the table and under it in the tree, documented per-thread versus whole-process counters with no double counting, an explicit capability limitation where no per-thread records exist, and the record, row and byte ceilings applied at and past the bound; no protocol, registry, SDK, renderer or client source change

entries.feature: Thread-aware source records with an explicit process/thread distinction: ProcessRecord::kind (user process with the kernel's thread count from stat field 20, kernel thread from PF_KTHREAD, or thread) and ProcessSnapshot::threads (NotProvided, NotRequested, or Read with its own unreadable and capped PID ledgers and denied count), so no process count ever counts a thread; a projection refuses a thread without its listed process, a process record naming a thread, and a thread record naming none

entries.feature: Thread identity: a thread's ProcessKey is its process instance's whole key plus ThreadIdentity { tid, creation }, the creation token being /proc/<pid>/task/<tid>/stat field 22 read with the thread's name and counters; a thread that ends loses its row and a new thread, including one reusing a TID, gets a new item ID while every other row keeps its own; the tree attaches a thread by that whole key, never by PID

entries.feature: Independent user-thread and kernel-thread visibility: standard checkbox Toggles Show user threads (node 75, off) and Show kernel threads (node 76, on) and a threads status Text (node 77) in a Row (node 74) between the view switch and the collections, disabled in the uncollected shell; each handler is its toggle's VALUE_CHANGED, an exact audit pair, which reads only the boolean and always publishes the value the server holds; showing user threads asks the loop for one sample that reads them, hiding them removes every thread row at once, clears an inspector on a thread and takes one sample without them; every real change of the user-thread setting discards a sample taken under the other setting and replaces it, including one Resume view or Refresh now asked for (merge verification F3, N1); hiding kernel threads samples nothing

entries.feature: Thread counts and the counter policy: the threads status counts threads by the kernel's count while hidden and thread rows while shown, each thread once; a process row is the whole process and a thread row that thread alone (its own CPU from task stat fields 14 and 15, Resident 'See process'), documented in the catalogue's metric definitions; per-thread CPU baselines are dropped with the process baselines when the boot or PID namespace changes, so a thread there warms up (Codex review); the summary's process count is the scan's process records

entries.feature: Hosts without reliable thread metadata: a source with no per-thread records (every fixture but --fake-threads, and ProcFsSource::live off Linux) states ThreadScan::NotProvided and the status says user threads are unavailable, never zero; a process whose task listing or a thread of which is unreadable or denied is named and counted and its earlier thread rows are kept; a source that does not classify kernel threads says so; earlier thread rows are kept only for the process instance this scan confirmed (whole key), never a process row, never a thread of an ended instance under a reused PID (correction round 1), and never an earlier thread instance under a TID this scan read under a new one (Codex review)
